title: AI Warning for Steam – Increases Visibility of AI Generated Content Disclosures
content:
AI warning for Steam is a browser extension and userscript that adds features to increase the visibility of AI Generated Content Disclosures in the Steam store.
- Display the AI Generated Content Disclosure on Steam store pages as a model popup on page load, if present.
- Blur or hide games with an AI Generated Content Disclosure on search pages in the Steam store.
AI warning for Steam can be installed as a native browser extension for Firefox or Chrome, or as a userscript for any supported browser. All variants run the exact same code, so installation and updates are the only differences.
This is the easier option, but updates can sometimes be delayed, because Mozilla and Google need to approve them first. (Usually this shouldn't take more than a day.) Just follow the appropriate link for your browser and click the install button.
This option is slightly less straight-forward, if you've never used a userscript, but you get updates as soon as they're available.
- If necessary, install a userscript manager for your browser. (Greasy Fork has instructions.)
- Click here to install the userscript or download aiwarningforsteam.user.js to install it manually.
The native browser extension should work in any up-to-date version of Firefox, Chrome, or any related browsers that can install extensions from the same sources, on any desktop OS. The Firefox version also works on mobile systems.
The userscript should work in any up-to-date browser with userscript support on any desktop or mobile OS.
The extension should work in all languages officially supported by the Steam store, but not all features are translated into languages other than English.
The purpose of this extension is to give users better visibility of information about whether generative AI was used in the creation of games they're browsing on Steam. Future updates might improve this functionality, but will not add unrelated features.

report.summary: A new browser extension and userscript for Steam makes AI-generated content disclosures more visible and lets users blur or hide disclosed games.
report.background: Generative AI has moved quickly into game development, from concept art and voice work to code and in-game assets. Valve began requiring Steam developers to disclose certain uses of generative AI on store pages, aiming to give players transparency while still allowing AI-assisted games. In practice, those disclosures can be easy to miss during normal browsing, especially on search results or crowded store pages. AI Warning for Steam is a community-built response: an unofficial browser extension and userscript that surfaces existing disclosures rather than judging whether AI use is good or bad. It reflects growing consumer interest in provenance and labeling as AI tools become more common in creative software.
key_points: On a Steam store page, the tool checks for an AI Generated Content Disclosure and, if one is present, shows it in a modal popup when the page loads. This turns a potentially buried notice into a visible prompt before users decide whether to learn more or wishlist the game.

On Steam search pages, the extension can blur or hide games that carry an AI disclosure. That gives users a quick way to filter their browsing, but it also means the tool depends entirely on the accuracy and completeness of Valve's disclosure system and developers' submissions.

The project is available as a native Firefox or Chrome extension and as a userscript for browsers with userscript support. All variants run the same code; the main difference is update speed, since browser-store approvals can delay extension releases while userscripts update immediately.

It is designed for desktop operating systems, with the Firefox version also working on mobile, and it supports Steam's official languages, though some features are not translated outside English. The stated scope is narrow: improve visibility of AI disclosures, with future updates intended to refine that function rather than add unrelated features.
report.impact: For regular users, the tool offers more agency: they can notice AI disclosures at a glance or avoid disclosed games in search results. For developers, it raises the reputational cost of using generative AI and could push studios toward clearer labeling or more cautious adoption. For the AI industry, it is a small but telling signal that provenance, consent, and labeling are becoming product features, not just policy debates. The caveat is that the extension is unofficial and only as reliable as Steam's disclosures; hiding games may also reinforce blanket assumptions about AI use.
report.tools: Follow the AI Warning for Steam GitHub repository for releases and issue updates. Install the native extension for Firefox or Chrome, or use a userscript manager such as Tampermonkey, Violentmonkey, or Greasemonkey to run aiwarningforsteam.user.js. Also compare against Valve's official Steam AI disclosure policy and store-page notices, since the tool only surfaces existing labels.
